_about: Tank (Track TK, 2026-10-10: mixed warfare). ALEX'S (decision mixed-warfare): 'You have a huge ship parked off the coast but you need tanks to move inland to spot the aa batteries for the ship', mobile artillery follows tanks later, each mission has only a few elements, ground objectives start closer and engagement ranges are not settled; shared spotting is yes (any friendly unit's sight counts for its side). The unit sheet's tank (reference/mockups/unit_sheet.html genTank: 5.6 to 6.6 m long, a turret with a gun 2.8 to 4.2 m long) is the drawing, and its engine-deck panel the side's accent zone (decision unit-sheet-choices). EVERYTHING ELSE HERE IS PROPOSED by Track TK. The planes' movement system with a tank's numbers: the same envelope (data/units/_schema.json) on the surface band, steered by PIVOT (one flat point in the turn curve: the tracks turn it at any speed), a top speed of 10 m/s which is its speed ON A ROAD; off the road it is slower and in woods slower still (the GROUND RULE, data/sim/ground.json: speed factors on this top speed, the climb of a height step only where a road crosses it, no river without an intact bridge, no water). Two steps a turn like the boats (the design doc: 'fast aircraft get several, tanks fewer'): a step is 2.5 s, 25 m on a road at top speed, 50 m a turn. ONE LIGHT GUN on its turret, firing on its own by the engagement rules (decision fire-by-engagement-parameters): the turret covers a FORWARD ARC of 170 degrees (ALEX, decision playtest-3: 'Tanks should have like a forward 170 arc. Not shoot directly behind.'; it was all the way round, Track TK's proposal), the cone is level (a few degrees up and down), so it engages what stands on the ground ahead of it, never a plane overhead. The main gun as a special is NOT built (Alex's decision big-guns-as-specials is for a warship's and artillery's guns). It carries no bombs and HAS NO SPECIALS (the orders card says so: 'no special: weapons fire on their own', builder CARD, decision playtest-3: a Special button that does nothing, with no word why, was Alex's 'no indication that it is engaged or why it won't engage').
name: Tank

size_m._reason: the unit sheet's tank is 5.6 to 6.6 m long (genTank length), 6 m is the middle; it is the same 6 m the effects boards draw as the tank for scale (scripts/fx/fx_board_strike.gd). Two thirds of a light fighter's 9 m span

draught_m._reason: a tank does not float: only a sea unit needs water under it. The ground rule keeps it OUT of water (data/sim/ground.json)

actions_per_turn._reason: design doc: 'give each unit type a number of decision points within it, so fast aircraft get several, tanks fewer'. Two a turn like the boats (2.5 s steps): a step is 25 m on a road at top speed, short enough that the ground rule samples it every few metres and the arc is the tank's own pivot turn, and few enough that planning a tank is not tedious

health._reason: armour: tougher than a patrol boat (5) and a heavy fighter (5), well under the bomber (8). The bombs (data/sim/bombs.json) take 3 for a hit within 12 m, 2 within 25 m, 1 within 45 m, so a tank dies to two direct hits or a good stick; its own light gun does 1 pip, so a tank takes six hits from another tank's gun

sight_range_m._reason: a tank commander's view from the turret (periscopes and the hatch): a little under the battery's 700 m and the fighters' 800, and well past its own gun's 350 m, so a tank SPOTS further than it shoots - which is the job Alex gave it, to spot the anti-aircraft batteries for the ship. Line of sight (data/view/fog.json vision.eye_height_m, ground 2.5 m) cuts it where a ridge or a cliff hides the ground

speed_min_mps._reason: slow reverse: a tank can reverse once stopped (design doc, Motion and inertia, 'ships can reverse once stopped', and the schema's reverse_from_stop for ships and tanks)

speed_cruise_mps._reason: a steady road march, a fifth below top speed (the AI drives at it and a new tank starts at it unless a scenario says otherwise). 8 m/s is about 29 km/h

speed_max_mps._reason: about 36 km/h: a WWII tank's road speed, and the speed ON A ROAD (the lead's brief for this track, not Alex's: about 10 m/s on a road, slower off it). Off the road the ground rule cuts it (data/sim/ground.json speed_factor)

dive_speed_max_mps._reason: a tank cannot dive: equal to speed_max_mps

accel_mps2._reason: from a stop to top speed in 5 s, one turn: a heavy hull with a big engine

decel_mps2._reason: brakes and the tracks' drag: from top speed to a stop in 2.5 s, one step, which is also what lets the ground rule slow it into woods or onto a shore within a step

reverse_from_stop._reason: design doc, Motion and inertia: ships and tanks reverse only once stopped; speed cannot cross zero within a step

turn_rate_curve_dps._reason: pivot steering (data/units/_schema.json: 'Tanks: one flat point'): the tracks turn it at the same rate at any speed, 30 deg/s, so a step turns it up to 75 degrees and a full circle takes 12 s (about two and a half turns). At top speed that is a turn radius of 19 m, three hull lengths

turn_bleed_mps2._reason: a tank loses a little speed in a hard turn (the track on the inside brakes): at the full rate 0.8 m/s per second, 2 m/s over a step

turn_bleed_exponent._reason: as the planes' and boats': gentle turns are nearly free, hard turns bite

altitude_bands._reason: it rides the ground: the surface band (data/sim/altitude.json). Bombs reach it (they hurt a unit at the surface)

hardpoints._reason: the turret's centre as the unit sheet draws it (turret_y -0.55 to -0.2 m, i.e. 0.4 m ahead of the hull's middle) and its height (hull 1.5 to 1.8 m plus half the turret's 0.75 to 0.95 m): about 2.3 m up. The same height the fog's eye is (data/view/fog.json eye_height_m, ground 2.5 m)

mount_deg._reason: the hull's front: the arc is centred on the nose (half_across_deg 85), so a tank fires on what is ahead of it and has to turn to face a target. Was 0 with an all-round cone, where the mount did not matter

half_across_deg._reason: ALEX (decision playtest-3, the third playtest, 2026-10-11): 'Tanks should have like a forward 170 arc. Not shoot directly behind.' So the light gun covers a FORWARD arc of 170 degrees: 85 either side of the hull's nose (mount_deg 0), the full width being 2 x 85 = 170. A target behind the tank, or beside it past 85 degrees, is out of the arc and is not fired on: the tank has to turn to bring it round (its pivot turn is 30 deg/s, so a step of 2.5 s turns it up to 75 degrees and a target dead astern takes two steps). The 'about' in Alex's 'like a forward 170' is taken as exactly 170 (PROPOSED reading; the number is data). Was 180, the turret traversing all the way round (PROPOSED by Track TK, never Alex's)

elevation_deg._reason: a level cone: a light gun on a tank engages what stands on the ground, centred on the horizon

half_height_deg._reason: ten degrees up and down of the level: the target's centre is on the ground (height 0) and the gun is 2.3 m up, so a target is in the cone from 13 m out (2.3 m / tan 10 deg), which is nearer than two hulls and a gun apart; and a hill's slope fits. Not enough for a plane: even a plane in the low band (120 m) is 19 degrees up at 350 m, so a tank never shoots at one (its reach is 420 m with the overshoot, where the low band is 16 degrees up). A tank cannot answer an air attack. (Was 6 in the first draft, which left a dead zone of 22 m round the hull.)

effective_range_m._reason: short and not settled (Alex: 'I am not sure what engagement ranges make sense yet'): well inside its own sight (600 m) and the battery's flak range, so a tank spots further than it shoots. A fighter's guns reach 450 m, a heavy cannon 600 m

base_hit_chance._reason: a light gun: 0.12 a roll, a tank on a target in range makes 0.12 hits a second before the other factors, 0.6 pips a turn; the odds are the engagement parameters' (decision fire-by-engagement-parameters), the balance is not calibrated (decision balance-uncalibrated)

rim_odds_factor._reason: flat: a turret gun is aimed by its gunner anywhere in the arc, like every turret and flexible gun

falloff_exponent._reason: no effect while the factor is flat (rim_odds_factor 1)

tracking_dps._reason: a powered turret tracks slower than a flexible machine gun (20 to 60) and a bomber's turrets (30): 12 deg/s. A target crossing at 10 m/s at 150 m is 3.8 deg/s, so it costs almost nothing, at 30 m it is 19 deg/s and the odds fall to a third

damage_pips._reason: one pip a hit like every other gun; the main gun (a special, not built) will hit harder

rolls_per_second._reason: one aimed shell a second: slower than a machine gun's two (a light gun loads between shots)
